summary: A summary of replies to the query in RFC 473 about MIX and MIXAL tools on the ARPANET. It lists rumored interpreters at Utah and Stanford, a MIXAL assembler and partly debugged interpreter at UCSB, and MIX and MIXAL on the UCSD B6700.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC summarizes replies to a question about MIX software on Network hosts. It separates confirmed reports from rumors and gives brief notes about each site.

questions: where could mix run on the arpanet
subtitle: A summary of reported locations for MIX and MIXAL software on the Network.

tldr.problem: RFC 473 asked whether ARPANET hosts offered an interpreter for MIX and an assembler for MIXAL.
tldr.mechanism: D. Walden summarizes replies and distinguishes reported availability from rumors about other hosts.
tldr.outcome: The RFC reports software at UCSB, UCSD, and UCLA, alongside rumors about Utah and SU-AI and a possible Stanford package.

sections.title: The Replies to the MIX Query
sections.content: David Walden summarizes responses to RFC 473, which asked whether network hosts had an assembler or interpreter for Knuth's hypothetical MIX computer. He first lists two unconfirmed reports: a MIX interpreter at the University of Utah and one at SU-AI.
sections.plainLanguage: The author groups the information into rumors and reported availability. The Utah and SU-AI entries are described as rumors.

sections.title: Reported Availability
sections.content:
The RFC reports a fairly well-debugged and documented MIXAL assembler and a partly debugged MIX interpreter at UCSB. It says MIX and MIXAL were available on the UCSD B6700, though they were not fully supported and might still have bugs.

It also reports that MIX and an assembler were available for network use on the UCLA 360/91 and had documentation.
sections.plainLanguage: The replies identify UCSB, UCSD, and UCLA as places where the tools could be found. The note also describes differences in how complete or supported they were.

sections.title: A Possible Stanford Package
sections.content: The final item says that Stanford University's Computer Science Center apparently had a standard package for exporting MIX systems to 360 and 370 computers. The RFC gives this as an apparent availability report rather than a detailed description.
sections.plainLanguage: The author also mentions a possible Stanford package for other computers. The note provides no further details about it.
